intro: You can already write a polite email, choose formal words and use the passive. Now let's put it all together: formal emails and letters that ask for information, complain and apply for a job, with the right opening and closing, and a short report with clear section headings.
teachingNotes: Build on the chain, recap each in a line, don't re-teach: b1-emails (the parts of an email, purpose in the first line, Could you …?, I'd be grateful if you could …, Dear Mr / Ms + surname, Dear Pak Budi with Indonesian colleagues, Best regards, Thank you for your time instead of 'Thank you for your attention'); b2-formal-informal-vocab (enquire / inquire, regarding, require, assist, inform you that …, phrasal verb → one Latin-based verb, match the reader; Yours sincerely / faithfully were only mentioned there, here they are taught and tested); b2-linking-words (However, Moreover, Consequently, As a result, despite, whereas); b2-passive-voice (the passive in every tense and after modals, It is said that …). New here: whole formal texts. Formal register = impersonal (objective, about facts, not feelings) and complete: no contractions; the passive where the doer is unknown, obvious or unimportant (The meeting has been postponed; Your application will be reviewed); formal words and linkers; one-word verbs instead of phrasal verbs; full sentences, no emoji, no abbreviations (pls, thx, asap, btw, info, docs), no !!!. These are tendencies: active sentences with I / we (I am writing to …, We have received your payment) are normal in formal letters; never mark a correct active sentence wrong, and don't push the passive into every sentence.

Letters by type (objective formal-emails-letters), purpose always in the first line. Request: I am writing to enquire about + topic (British; inquire = American) — the node's common error 'I want to ask about the training schedule.' → 'I am writing to enquire about the training schedule.' ('I want' is correct English but too direct for a formal letter; 'I would like to ask about' is fine in a semi-formal email); I would be grateful if you could + base verb; Could you please …?; I would like to request …; 'enquire the fees' ✗ → enquire about. Complaint, firm but polite, three steps: the problem (I am writing to complain about …), the facts (dates, order / booking number, what already happened: On 2 May I ordered … However, …), the action you expect (I would appreciate a refund / a replacement; I would be grateful if you could resolve this matter by …); no capitals, no !!!, no threats. Application: I am writing to apply for the position of + job, as advertised on + place ('as advertised on' is a phrase to remember: don't explain it as a reduced clause); apply FOR a job / TO a company; experience (I have three years' experience in …); Please find attached my CV (a fixed phrase, = Terlampir) or I have attached my CV; I would welcome the opportunity to discuss my application at an interview.

Openings and closings. Dear Mr / Ms + surname, (Dear Pak Hasan, / Dear Bu Ani, with Indonesian colleagues) … Yours sincerely, (name known); Dear Sir or Madam, (also Dear Sir/Madam,) … Yours faithfully, (name unknown). This is the British convention; trick: Sir and sincerely never go together. American English uses Sincerely, (or Sincerely yours,) in both cases and rarely Yours faithfully: accept Sincerely as correct American usage, but when a task says British, the answer is the British pair. Kind regards, / Best regards, are the normal sign-offs in semi-formal work emails (and many formal emails today): never mark them wrong in a free email, just say Yours sincerely / faithfully is the more formal letter style. Usually only Y is capital (Yours sincerely,). Indonesian letter habits to name: Kepada Yth. … / Dengan hormat, → one greeting line only (no English line for Dengan hormat; 'With respect,' ✗); long openings (Puji syukur …, Semoga Bapak/Ibu senantiasa dalam keadaan sehat, praise of the company) → leave out and state the purpose; Saya yang bertanda tangan di bawah ini → leave out; Demikian surat ini kami sampaikan. Atas perhatiannya kami ucapkan terima kasih. → Thank you for your time. I look forward to hearing from you. ('Thus this letter we convey' ✗); Hormat kami, → Yours sincerely / faithfully. Stiff Indonesian office English: 'Please be informed that …', 'Herewith we send …', 'Kindly …' → We would like to inform you that …, Please find attached / I have attached …, Could you please …?

Short report (objective structure-a-short). The learner met report sections in b2-reading-strategies (summary, findings, recommendations): recap in a line. A report has a title and short noun headings, no Dear and no sign-off. Introduction = the aim in one or two sentences (The aim / purpose of this report is to + verb …; This report looks at …). Findings = facts and numbers, often in the passive (A survey was conducted …, It was found that …, Several complaints were received …) with linkers (However, Moreover, As a result). Recommendations = what should happen next (The company should …; It is recommended that + subject + verb …: a formal phrase to remember; use plural subjects in examples so the verb form doesn't need explaining: It is recommended that staff use the new app; if asked, say British English also writes 'should': It is recommended that the canteen should open earlier). Some reports add a Conclusion. Bullet points are fine. Each section has one job: no recommendations in the Findings, no new facts in the Recommendations; objective tone (no I think, no feelings, no !!!). Indonesian trap: school and campus reports (BAB I Pendahuluan, Latar Belakang, Rumusan Masalah) are long; an English short report goes straight to the point.

Limits: A0–B1 grammar plus the chain (all passive tenses, B2 linkers, formal vocabulary, phrasal verbs and idioms). No inversion (Should you require …), no participle clauses (Having received …, Referring to …), no non-defining relative clauses (…, which …), no third conditional or wish, no past modals. Don't teach hereby, herewith, aforementioned, henceforth or 'Please be informed': if the learner uses them, accept them and say they sound old-fashioned. Typed answers are lowercased and stripped of punctuation, so commas after the greeting and sign-off can't be graded in the checkpoint: give feedback on them in the free writing practice. When the learner writes a full email or report, praise the structure first, then correct ONE thing (usually the sign-off, a contraction, 'I want to ask about', or a section with the wrong content). Contexts: Jakarta / Bandung / Surabaya offices, startups, universities abroad, scholarships, online shops, hotels, JobStreet and LinkedIn ads.

keyPoints.title: What makes writing formal
keyPoints.explanation: Formal English is impersonal (about the facts, not your feelings) and complete: no contractions (I am, we cannot), the passive when the doer isn't important (The meeting has been postponed.), formal words and linkers (enquire, regarding, require; However, Moreover), one-word verbs instead of phrasal verbs (postpone, not put off) and full sentences with no emoji or abbreviations (as soon as possible, not asap). These are tendencies: active sentences with I or we (I am writing …, We have received …) are fine too.

examples.en: The meeting has been postponed until next Tuesday.
We cannot accept applications after 30 June.
examples.id: Kami tidak dapat menerima lamaran setelah 30 Juni.

examples.en: Thank you for the information. I will check it tomorrow.
examples.id: Terima kasih atas informasinya. Saya akan memeriksanya besok.

id.title: Apa yang membuat tulisan jadi formal
id.explanation: Bahasa Inggris formal itu impersonal (tentang fakta, bukan perasaanmu) dan lengkap: tanpa kontraksi (I am, we cannot), kalimat pasif kalau pelakunya tidak penting (The meeting has been postponed.), kata dan kata penghubung formal (enquire, regarding, require; However, Moreover), kata kerja satu kata sebagai ganti phrasal verb (postpone, bukan put off), dan kalimat lengkap tanpa emoji atau singkatan (as soon as possible, bukan asap). Ini kecenderungan: kalimat aktif dengan I atau we (I am writing …, We have received …) juga tidak masalah.

keyPoints.title: Formal emails and letters: request, complaint, application
keyPoints.explanation: Say your purpose in the first line. Request: I am writing to enquire about … and I would be grateful if you could … Complaint: the problem (I am writing to complain about …), the facts (dates, order number), then the action you expect (I would appreciate a replacement.). Application: I am writing to apply for the position of …, as advertised on … Open with Dear Mr / Ms + surname and close with Yours sincerely, or, after Dear Sir or Madam, with Yours faithfully, (British; American English uses Sincerely,). Kind regards, suits semi-formal emails.

examples.en: I am writing to enquire about internships at your company.
examples.id: Saya menulis untuk menanyakan program magang di perusahaan Anda.

examples.en: I am writing to apply for the position of Data Analyst, as advertised on LinkedIn.
examples.id: Saya bermaksud melamar posisi Data Analyst, sesuai iklan di LinkedIn.

examples.en: I would be grateful if you could resolve this matter by 15 May.
examples.id: Saya akan sangat berterima kasih jika Anda dapat menyelesaikan masalah ini paling lambat 15 Mei.

id.title: Email dan surat formal: permintaan, keluhan, lamaran
id.explanation: Sebutkan tujuanmu di kalimat pertama. Permintaan: I am writing to enquire about … dan I would be grateful if you could … Keluhan: masalahnya (I am writing to complain about …), faktanya (tanggal, nomor pesanan), lalu tindakan yang kamu harapkan (I would appreciate a replacement.). Lamaran: I am writing to apply for the position of …, as advertised on … Buka dengan Dear Mr / Ms + nama keluarga dan tutup dengan Yours sincerely, atau, setelah Dear Sir or Madam, dengan Yours faithfully, (British; bahasa Inggris Amerika memakai Sincerely,). Kind regards, cocok untuk email semi-formal.

keyPoints.title: A short report with headings
keyPoints.explanation: A report has a title and section headings, with no greeting and no sign-off. Introduction: the aim (The aim of this report is to …). Findings: the facts and numbers, often in the passive (A survey was conducted …, It was found that …). Recommendations: what should happen next (The company should …, It is recommended that …). Keep it objective: facts, not feelings.

examples.en: The aim of this report is to assess the new English classes for staff.
examples.id: Tujuan laporan ini adalah menilai kelas bahasa Inggris baru untuk karyawan.

examples.en: A survey was conducted in March, and 60 staff took part.
examples.id: Survei dilakukan pada bulan Maret, dan 60 karyawan ikut serta.

examples.en: The classes should start at 4.30 p.m. instead.

id.title: Laporan singkat dengan judul bagian
id.explanation: Laporan punya judul dan judul bagian (heading), tanpa salam pembuka dan tanpa salam penutup. Introduction: tujuannya (The aim of this report is to …). Findings: fakta dan angka, sering dalam kalimat pasif (A survey was conducted …, It was found that …). Recommendations: apa yang sebaiknya dilakukan selanjutnya (The company should …, It is recommended that …). Tetap objektif: fakta, bukan perasaan.

guidedPractice.prompt: Rewrite for a formal notice, in the passive without the doer (same tense): 'We have moved the seminar to Room 4.'
expected: the seminar has been moved to room 4
guidedPractice.hint: has / have been + third form. In a notice the doer (we) isn't important, so leave it out: The seminar has been moved to Room 4.

guidedPractice.prompt: Make this sentence from a report formal: no contraction, and one formal verb instead of find out. 'We couldn't find out the cause of the problem.'
expected: we could not discover the cause of the problem
we were unable to discover the cause of the problem
we could not identify the cause of the problem
we could not determine the cause of the problem
we were unable to identify the cause of the problem
guidedPractice.hint: couldn't → could not (or were unable to); find out → discover (or identify).

guidedPractice.prompt: You're writing a formal letter to a company, but you don't know who will read it. Write the greeting (a comma is optional).
guidedPractice.hint: No name → Dear Sir or Madam (also written Dear Sir/Madam). Then, in British English, the letter ends with Yours faithfully.

guidedPractice.prompt: A hotel in Yogyakarta charged your card twice for one night. In your complaint email, write the sentence that says what you expect. Start with I would appreciate.
expected: i would appreciate a refund of the second payment
i would appreciate a refund of the extra payment
i would appreciate a refund of the second charge
i would appreciate a refund of the extra charge
i would appreciate a full refund of the second payment
guidedPractice.hint: The last step of a complaint is the action you expect: I would appreciate + a noun (a refund of the extra payment).

guidedPractice.prompt: Write the three headings of a short report, in order.
guidedPractice.hint: The aim → the facts → what should happen next: Introduction, Findings, Recommendations.

independentPractice.prompt: Write a formal complaint email (100–150 words) to an online electronics shop. You ordered a laptop on 3 June (order no. 77120). It arrived ten days late, and the keyboard does not work. Checklist: Dear Sir or Madam; the purpose in the first line; the facts; the action you expect; a closing line; Yours faithfully + your name; no contractions, no !!!
expected: i am writing to complain about
i look forward to hearing from you
independentPractice.hint: Rubric: purpose in the first line (I am writing to complain about …); the facts with the date and order number; a clear action (I would appreciate a replacement / a refund; I would be grateful if you could … by …); calm, formal style (no contractions, no capitals for anger); Dear Sir or Madam … Yours faithfully.

independentPractice.prompt: Write a short application email (100–150 words) to Ms Rachel Lim, HR Manager at a logistics company in Singapore, for the position of Customer Service Officer, advertised on LinkedIn. Mention your experience and your CV.
expected: i am writing to apply for the position of customer service officer
i have three years experience in
i would welcome the opportunity to discuss my application at an interview
independentPractice.hint: Rubric: Dear Ms Lim (not Dear Ms Rachel); purpose first (I am writing to apply for the position of …, as advertised on LinkedIn); one short paragraph on experience and skills; the CV (Please find attached my CV / I have attached my CV); a closing line; Yours sincerely (name known); no contractions.

independentPractice.prompt: Your manager wants a short report (120–180 words) on the office's new hybrid schedule (two days at home, three in the office). Write a title and three sections with headings. Include two findings with numbers and two recommendations.
expected: report on the new hybrid schedule
the aim of this report is to
independentPractice.hint: Rubric: a title; Introduction = the aim in 1–2 sentences; Findings = facts and numbers only (the passive helps: A survey was conducted …); Recommendations = should / It is recommended that …; no Dear, no sign-off; objective style (no I think, no !!!).

assessment.prompt: Rewrite this sentence from a company notice in a formal register: use the passive without the doer, keep the same tense, and use no contractions. 'We've cancelled the staff conference because of the floods.'
acceptableAnswers: the staff conference has been cancelled because of the floods
the staff conference has been canceled because of the floods
the staff conference has been cancelled due to the floods
the staff conference has been canceled due to the floods
the staff conference has been cancelled owing to the floods
the staff conference has been cancelled as a result of the floods
because of the floods the staff conference has been cancelled
due to the floods the staff conference has been cancelled
due to the floods the staff conference has been canceled
assessment.rubric: Correct: The staff conference has been cancelled because of / due to the floods (has been + third form; canceled is the American spelling). 'The staff conference was cancelled …' = 80 (a correct passive, but the tense changed). 'The staff conference's been cancelled …' = 70 (a contraction). '… has been cancelled by us …' = 60 (the doer isn't needed). 'has been cancel' = 40. The active sentence unchanged = 0.

assessment.prompt: Rewrite this line for a formal email to a new client: a polite request in full words, with no abbreviations. 'Pls send the docs asap.'
acceptableAnswers: please send the documents as soon as possible
please send me the documents as soon as possible
please send us the documents as soon as possible
could you please send the documents as soon as possible
could you please send me the documents as soon as possible
could you please send us the documents as soon as possible
could you send the documents as soon as possible
could you send me the documents as soon as possible
could you send us the documents as soon as possible
could you send the documents as soon as possible please
please could you send the documents as soon as possible
would you please send the documents as soon as possible
i would be grateful if you could send the documents as soon as possible
i would be grateful if you could send me the documents as soon as possible
i would be grateful if you could send us the documents as soon as possible
assessment.rubric: Correct: Please send / Could you (please) send / I would be grateful if you could send + the documents + as soon as possible. Any abbreviation left (pls, docs, asap or ASAP) = 50. 'Send the documents as soon as possible.' = 60 (full words, but an order with no please). 'I want the documents as soon as possible.' = 40 (too direct). 'Kindly send the documents as soon as possible.' = 80 (formal, but it still sounds like an order).

assessment.prompt: Rewrite this first line of an email to a university in Australia in a formal style, using enquire: 'I want to ask about your scholarships for Indonesian students.'
acceptableAnswers: i am writing to enquire about your scholarships for indonesian students
i am writing to inquire about your scholarships for indonesian students
i would like to enquire about your scholarships for indonesian students
i would like to inquire about your scholarships for indonesian students
i am writing to enquire about the scholarships for indonesian students
i am writing to inquire about the scholarships for indonesian students
i am writing to enquire about scholarships for indonesian students
i am writing to inquire about scholarships for indonesian students
assessment.rubric: Correct: I am writing to enquire about your scholarships for Indonesian students (inquire is the American spelling; I would like to enquire about … = 100). 'I'm writing to enquire …' = 80 (a contraction in a formal letter). 'I want to enquire about …' = 60 (want sounds too direct). 'I am writing to enquire your scholarships …' = 50 (enquire about + topic). 'I would like to ask about …' = 60 (polite, but the task asks for enquire). Unchanged = 0.

assessment.prompt: You're writing a formal letter in British English to the HR manager of a company in London. It starts 'Dear Ms Carter,'. Which sign-off goes at the end: Yours sincerely or Yours faithfully?
acceptableAnswers: yours sincerely
assessment.rubric: Correct: Yours sincerely (British: you know the reader's name). 'Yours faithfully' = 0 (that goes with Dear Sir or Madam). 'Sincerely' or 'Sincerely yours' = 70 (the American style; this letter is British). 'Kind regards' = 50 (fine in a semi-formal email, but not one of the two choices).

assessment.prompt: Complete the first line of a job application email with one word: 'I am writing to apply for the position of Sales Executive at PT Maju Jaya, as ___ on JobStreet on 3 June.'
acceptableAnswers: advertised
posted
listed
assessment.rubric: Correct: advertised (as advertised on … is the standard phrase in applications). 'posted' or 'listed' = 100. 'advertise' or 'advertising' = 40 (wrong form). 'seen' = 40 ('as seen on' is for products in adverts, not job ads). 'informed' or 'announced' = 20.

assessment.prompt: A short report on the staff shuttle bus has three headings: Introduction, Findings and Recommendations. Under which heading does this paragraph go? Write the heading. 'A second bus should be added at 7 a.m. It is also recommended that drivers check the air conditioning every week.'
acceptableAnswers: recommendations
recommendation
under recommendations
the recommendations section
assessment.rubric: Correct: Recommendations (should and It is recommended that say what should happen next). 'Findings' = 0 (findings are facts and numbers from the survey, not suggestions). 'Introduction' = 0 (the introduction gives the aim of the report). 'Conclusion' = 40 (some reports have one, but it isn't one of the three headings here).

assessment.prompt: Complete the first sentence of a report's Introduction with one formal word: 'The ___ of this report is to compare two cloud storage services and recommend one for the company.'
acceptableAnswers: aim
purpose
objective
assessment.rubric: Correct: aim (The aim of this report is to …). 'purpose' or 'objective' = 100. 'goal' = 80 (correct, a little less formal). 'reason' = 50. 'target' or 'point' = 30.

id.title: Apa yang membuat bahasa Inggris formal?

blocks.text:
Quick recap: from B1 you know the parts of an email (the purpose first, *Could you …?*, *Best regards,*). In the last lessons you learnt formal words (*enquire, regarding, require*), formal linkers (*However, Moreover, Consequently*) and the passive in every tense. A formal email, letter or report puts them all together. It sounds **impersonal** (objective and calm: about the facts, not about your feelings) and **complete**:
- **No contractions** (short forms): *I am, we cannot, it is, do not*
- **The passive** when the doer isn't important or is obvious: *The meeting has been postponed.* *Your application will be reviewed.*
- **Formal words and linkers**: *enquire, regarding, require, assist; However, Moreover, Consequently*
- **One-word verbs** instead of phrasal verbs: *postpone* (not *put off*), *investigate* (not *look into*)
- **Full sentences**: no emoji, no abbreviations like *pls, thx, asap, btw, info*, no *!!!*

These are **tendencies**, not laws. Active sentences with *I* or *we* are normal in formal letters: *I am writing to …*, *We have received your payment.* Use the passive where it helps, not in every sentence.

id.text:
Ulasan singkat: dari B1 kamu sudah tahu bagian-bagian email (tujuan di awal, *Could you …?*, *Best regards,*). Di pelajaran-pelajaran terakhir kamu belajar kata formal (*enquire, regarding, require*), kata penghubung formal (*However, Moreover, Consequently*) dan kalimat pasif di semua tense. Email, surat atau laporan formal menggabungkan semuanya. Bunyinya **impersonal** (objektif dan tenang: tentang fakta, bukan tentang perasaanmu) dan **lengkap**:
- **Tanpa kontraksi** (bentuk singkat): *I am, we cannot, it is, do not*
- **Kalimat pasif** kalau pelakunya tidak penting atau sudah jelas: *The meeting has been postponed.* *Your application will be reviewed.*
- **Kata dan kata penghubung formal**: *enquire, regarding, require, assist; However, Moreover, Consequently*
- **Kata kerja satu kata** sebagai ganti phrasal verb: *postpone* (bukan *put off*), *investigate* (bukan *look into*)
- **Kalimat lengkap**: tanpa emoji, tanpa singkatan seperti *pls, thx, asap, btw, info*, tanpa *!!!*

Ini **kecenderungan**, bukan hukum. Kalimat aktif dengan *I* atau *we* biasa saja di surat formal: *I am writing to …*, *We have received your payment.* Pakai pasif kalau memang membantu, bukan di setiap kalimat. Surat resmi bahasa Indonesia juga sering memakai bentuk pasif (*dilampirkan, telah diterima*), jadi gaya ini sebenarnya tidak asing untukmu.

rows.en: We've put off the meeting till next Tuesday.
rows.id: Kami menunda rapatnya sampai Selasa depan.
rows.note: informal: a contraction, a phrasal verb, till

rows.en: The meeting has been postponed until next Tuesday.
rows.id: Rapatnya ditunda sampai Selasa depan.
rows.note: formal: the passive, a one-word verb, until

id.note: formal: kalimat pasif, kata kerja satu kata, until

rows.en: Sorry, can't make it on Fri!!
rows.id: Maaf, nggak bisa datang hari Jumat!!

rows.en: Unfortunately, I am unable to attend the meeting on Friday.
rows.id: Sayangnya, saya tidak dapat menghadiri rapat hari Jumat.
rows.note: formal: a full sentence, no contraction

rows.en: Thx for the info, will check it tmrw.
rows.id: Makasih infonya, besok aku cek.

rows.en: Thank you for the information. I will check it tomorrow.
rows.id: Terima kasih atas informasinya. Saya akan memeriksanya besok.

rows.en: Your parcel will be delivered within three working days.
rows.id: Paket Anda akan dikirim dalam tiga hari kerja.
rows.note: formal: the passive, because the doer (the courier) isn't important

id.note: formal: pasif, karena pelakunya (kurir) tidak penting

blocks.text: **Formal doesn't mean old-fashioned.** Indonesian office English often uses stiff phrases translated from letters: *Please be informed that …* (from *Dengan ini kami informasikan*), *Herewith we send …* (from *Bersama ini kami kirimkan*), *Kindly …*. They sound old-fashioned, or like an order. Clear, modern formal English is better: *We would like to inform you that …*, *Please find attached …* / *I have attached …*, *Could you please …?*. And *I want to …* is correct English, but in a formal letter it sounds too direct: write *I would like to …*.

id.text: **Formal bukan berarti kuno.** Bahasa Inggris di kantor Indonesia sering memakai frasa kaku yang diterjemahkan dari surat: *Please be informed that …* (dari *Dengan ini kami informasikan*), *Herewith we send …* (dari *Bersama ini kami kirimkan*), *Kindly …*. Frasa ini terdengar kuno, atau seperti perintah. Bahasa Inggris formal yang jelas dan modern lebih baik: *We would like to inform you that …*, *Please find attached …* / *I have attached …*, *Could you please …?*. Dan *I want to …* itu bahasa Inggris yang benar, tapi di surat formal terdengar terlalu langsung: tulis *I would like to …*.

blocks.prompt: Which sentence fits a formal letter from a bank to its customers?
options: Your new card's been sent, pls check your mailbox!
Your new card has been sent to your registered address.
We sent off your new card, so check your mailbox.
blocks.explain: A formal letter uses full forms, the passive (the bank is obviously the doer) and no abbreviations: **Your new card has been sent to your registered address.** The first has a contraction (*card's*), *pls* and *!*; the third uses the phrasal verb *sent off* and sounds like a chat.

id.prompt: Kalimat mana yang cocok untuk surat formal dari bank kepada nasabahnya?
id.explain: Surat formal memakai bentuk lengkap, kalimat pasif (pelakunya jelas bank) dan tanpa singkatan: **Your new card has been sent to your registered address.** Pilihan pertama punya kontraksi (*card's*), *pls* dan *!*; pilihan ketiga memakai phrasal verb *sent off* dan terdengar seperti chat.

blocks.text:
**Greeting** (the first line):
- You know the name: **Dear Mr / Ms + surname** (family name): *Dear Ms Tan,* (not *Dear Ms Lina* ✗). With Indonesian colleagues: *Dear Pak Hasan,* / *Dear Bu Ani,*.
- You don't know the name: **Dear Sir or Madam,** (also written *Dear Sir/Madam,*).

**Opening line**: your purpose, straight away: *I am writing to …*

**Closing line**: *Thank you for your time.* / *I look forward to hearing from you.* (look forward to + -ing: a phrase you know)

**Sign-off** (the last words before your name) + your full name on the next line. In formal **British** letters and emails:
- after *Dear Ms Tan,* (name known) → **Yours sincerely,**
- after *Dear Sir or Madam,* (name unknown) → **Yours faithfully,**

The trick: **S**ir and **s**incerely never go together. **American** English usually ends with **Sincerely,** (or *Sincerely yours,*) in both cases; *Yours faithfully* is rare there. In ordinary work emails, even polite ones, **Kind regards,** or **Best regards,** is normal: that's semi-formal. Usually only the *Y* is a capital letter: *Yours sincerely,*.

id.text:
**Salam pembuka** (baris pertama):
- Kamu tahu namanya: **Dear Mr / Ms + surname** (nama keluarga): *Dear Ms Tan,* (bukan *Dear Ms Lina* ✗). Dengan rekan kerja orang Indonesia: *Dear Pak Hasan,* / *Dear Bu Ani,*.
- Kamu tidak tahu namanya: **Dear Sir or Madam,** (juga ditulis *Dear Sir/Madam,*).

**Kalimat pembuka**: langsung sebutkan tujuanmu: *I am writing to …*

**Kalimat penutup**: *Thank you for your time.* / *I look forward to hearing from you.* (look forward to + -ing: frasa yang sudah kamu kenal)

**Salam penutup** (kata terakhir sebelum namamu) + nama lengkapmu di baris berikutnya. Di surat dan email formal **British**:
- setelah *Dear Ms Tan,* (nama diketahui) → **Yours sincerely,**
- setelah *Dear Sir or Madam,* (nama tidak diketahui) → **Yours faithfully,**

Triknya: **S**ir dan **s**incerely tidak pernah berpasangan. Bahasa Inggris **Amerika** biasanya menutup dengan **Sincerely,** (atau *Sincerely yours,*) untuk keduanya; *Yours faithfully* jarang dipakai di sana. Di email kerja sehari-hari, meskipun sopan, **Kind regards,** atau **Best regards,** itu biasa: itu semi-formal. Biasanya hanya huruf *Y* yang kapital: *Yours sincerely,*.

blocks.text:
**Indonesian letter habits to drop.**
- *Kepada Yth. … / Dengan hormat,* → just one line: *Dear Ms Tan,*. English has no line for *Dengan hormat* (*With respect,* ✗: people say *with all due respect* just before they disagree!).
- *Puji syukur …*, *Semoga Bapak/Ibu senantiasa dalam keadaan sehat*, a paragraph praising the company → leave it out (at most a short *I hope you are well.* in a semi-formal email) and start with your purpose.
- *Saya yang bertanda tangan di bawah ini …* → leave it out: your name is under the sign-off.
- *Demikian surat ini kami sampaikan. Atas perhatiannya kami ucapkan terima kasih.* → **Thank you for your time. I look forward to hearing from you.** (not *Thus this letter we convey* ✗)
- *Hormat kami,* → *Yours sincerely,* / *Yours faithfully,* / *Kind regards,*

id.text:
**Kebiasaan surat Indonesia yang perlu ditinggalkan.**
- *Kepada Yth. … / Dengan hormat,* → cukup satu baris: *Dear Ms Tan,*. Bahasa Inggris tidak punya baris untuk *Dengan hormat* (*With respect,* ✗: orang mengucapkan *with all due respect* justru sebelum menyatakan tidak setuju!).
- *Puji syukur …*, *Semoga Bapak/Ibu senantiasa dalam keadaan sehat*, satu paragraf memuji perusahaan → hapus saja (paling banyak *I hope you are well.* yang singkat di email semi-formal) dan mulai dengan tujuanmu.
- *Saya yang bertanda tangan di bawah ini …* → hapus saja: namamu sudah ada di bawah salam penutup.
- *Demikian surat ini kami sampaikan. Atas perhatiannya kami ucapkan terima kasih.* → **Thank you for your time. I look forward to hearing from you.** (bukan *Thus this letter we convey* ✗)
- *Hormat kami,* → *Yours sincerely,* / *Yours faithfully,* / *Kind regards,*

blocks.prompt: Rina translated the end of her Indonesian letter word for word. Which ending is natural in English?
options: Thank you for your time. I look forward to hearing from you.
Thus this letter we convey. For your attention we say thank you.
With respect, thank you for your attention.
blocks.explain: *Demikian surat ini kami sampaikan …* has no word-for-word English version. A formal English letter simply ends with **Thank you for your time. I look forward to hearing from you.** *With respect* isn't an English letter phrase, and *Thank you for your attention* sounds like the end of a presentation.

id.prompt: Rina menerjemahkan bagian akhir surat bahasa Indonesianya kata per kata. Penutup mana yang wajar dalam bahasa Inggris?
id.explain: *Demikian surat ini kami sampaikan …* tidak punya versi bahasa Inggris kata per kata. Surat formal bahasa Inggris cukup ditutup dengan **Thank you for your time. I look forward to hearing from you.** *With respect* bukan frasa surat bahasa Inggris, dan *Thank you for your attention* terdengar seperti akhir presentasi.

blocks.text:
Each kind of letter has its own plan. In all of them, **the purpose comes in the first line**.

**1. A request** (e.g. information from a university, a hotel or a company)
- Open: *I am writing to **enquire about** …* (British; American *inquire*). *I want to ask about …* is correct English, but in a formal letter it sounds too direct and too simple.
- Ask: *I would be grateful if you could* + base verb … (a phrase you know from B1), *Could you please …?*, *I would like to request …*
- Close: *Thank you for your time. I look forward to hearing from you.*

**2. A complaint**: firm but polite, in three steps:
- **the problem**: *I am writing to complain about …*
- **the facts**: what happened, when, the order or booking number, what you have already done: *On 2 May I ordered … However, …*
- **the action you expect**: *I would appreciate a replacement.* *I would be grateful if you could resolve this matter by 15 May.*
No CAPITALS, no *!!!*, no insults: calm facts are stronger.

**3. A job application** (often with a CV)
- Open: *I am writing to apply for the position of* + the job, *as advertised on* + the place: *… of Data Analyst, as advertised on LinkedIn.* (*as advertised on* = sesuai iklan di: a phrase to remember)
- Body: your experience and skills: *I have three years' experience in …*, *I am currently studying …*
- Attach: *Please find attached my CV.* (a fixed phrase) or *I have attached my CV.*
- Close: *I would welcome the opportunity to discuss my application at an interview.*

id.text:
Setiap jenis surat punya rencananya sendiri. Di semuanya, **tujuan ada di kalimat pertama**.

**1. Permintaan** (request; misalnya informasi dari universitas, hotel atau perusahaan)
- Pembuka: *I am writing to **enquire about** …* (British; Amerika *inquire*). *I want to ask about …* itu bahasa Inggris yang benar, tapi di surat formal terdengar terlalu langsung dan terlalu sederhana.
- Meminta: *I would be grateful if you could* + kata kerja dasar … (frasa yang kamu kenal dari B1), *Could you please …?*, *I would like to request …*
- Penutup: *Thank you for your time. I look forward to hearing from you.*

**2. Keluhan** (complaint): tegas tapi sopan, dalam tiga langkah:
- **masalahnya**: *I am writing to complain about …*
- **faktanya**: apa yang terjadi, kapan, nomor pesanan atau pemesanan, apa yang sudah kamu lakukan: *On 2 May I ordered … However, …*
- **tindakan yang kamu harapkan**: *I would appreciate a replacement.* *I would be grateful if you could resolve this matter by 15 May.*
Tanpa HURUF KAPITAL semua, tanpa *!!!*, tanpa hinaan: fakta yang tenang justru lebih kuat.

**3. Lamaran kerja** (job application; sering dengan CV)
- Pembuka: *I am writing to apply for the position of* + pekerjaannya, *as advertised on* + tempatnya: *… of Data Analyst, as advertised on LinkedIn.* (*as advertised on* = sesuai iklan di: frasa yang dihafal saja)
- Isi: pengalaman dan keahlianmu: *I have three years' experience in …*, *I am currently studying …*
- Lampiran: *Please find attached my CV.* (frasa tetap, = Terlampir CV saya) atau *I have attached my CV.*
- Penutup: *I would welcome the opportunity to discuss my application at an interview.*

blocks.text:
**Indonesian traps.**
1) *Saya ingin menanyakan …* → *I want to ask about …* sounds too direct in a formal letter. The classic: *I want to ask about the training schedule.* → **I am writing to enquire about the training schedule.**
2) **enquire about** + a topic: *enquire about the fees*, not *enquire the fees* ✗.
3) *Mohon segera ditindaklanjuti* → not *Please follow up immediately!* (an order) → *I would be grateful if you could resolve this matter as soon as possible.*
4) *melamar posisi* → **apply for** the position (not *apply the position* ✗); *to* is for the company: *apply to PT Maju Jaya*.
5) *Bersama ini saya lampirkan …* → *Please find attached …* / *I have attached …* (*Herewith I attach …* sounds old-fashioned).

id.text:
**Jebakan untuk penutur bahasa Indonesia.**
1) *Saya ingin menanyakan …* → *I want to ask about …* terdengar terlalu langsung di surat formal. Contoh klasiknya: *I want to ask about the training schedule.* → **I am writing to enquire about the training schedule.**
2) **enquire about** + topik: *enquire about the fees*, bukan *enquire the fees* ✗.
3) *Mohon segera ditindaklanjuti* → bukan *Please follow up immediately!* (itu perintah) → *I would be grateful if you could resolve this matter as soon as possible.*
4) *melamar posisi* → **apply for** the position (bukan *apply the position* ✗); *to* untuk perusahaannya: *apply to PT Maju Jaya*.
5) *Bersama ini saya lampirkan …* → *Please find attached …* / *I have attached …* (*Herewith I attach …* terdengar kuno).

blocks.prompt: Sari's new phone stopped working after two days. Which sentence from her complaint email says the action she expects?
options: I am very disappointed with your service.
The phone stopped working after only two days.
I would be grateful if you could replace the phone by 20 June.
blocks.explain: The action she expects is what she wants the shop to do: **I would be grateful if you could replace the phone by 20 June.** The second sentence gives the facts, and the first only shows a feeling: both are useful, but neither tells the shop what to do.

id.prompt: Ponsel baru Sari rusak setelah dua hari. Kalimat mana dari email keluhannya yang menyebutkan tindakan yang ia harapkan?
id.explain: Tindakan yang diharapkan adalah apa yang ia ingin toko lakukan: **I would be grateful if you could replace the phone by 20 June.** Kalimat kedua memberi faktanya, dan kalimat pertama hanya menunjukkan perasaan: keduanya berguna, tapi tidak ada yang memberi tahu toko apa yang harus dilakukan.

blocks.text:
In B2 reading you met long reports with a summary, findings and recommendations. Now you write a **short** one, for example for your manager after a survey. A report is not a letter: **no Dear …, no sign-off**. It has a **title** and **section headings** (a short name above each part), so the reader can jump to the part they need:
- **Title**: *Report on the new English classes for staff*
- **Introduction**: the **aim** in one or two sentences: *The aim of this report is to …* / *This report looks at …*
- **Findings**: the facts and numbers. The passive keeps it objective: *A survey was conducted …*, *It was found that …*, *Several complaints were received …*. Linkers show the logic: *However, Moreover, As a result,*
- **Recommendations**: what should happen next: *The company should …*, *It is recommended that* + subject + verb (a formal phrase to remember: *It is recommended that staff use the new app.*)

Some reports add a **Conclusion** before the recommendations, and bullet points are fine. Keep it **objective**: facts and numbers, not feelings (*I think …*, *terrible!!*). Your own view appears only as recommendations.

id.text:
Di pelajaran membaca B2 kamu sudah bertemu laporan panjang dengan ringkasan, temuan dan rekomendasi. Sekarang kamu menulis laporan **singkat**, misalnya untuk atasanmu setelah survei. Laporan bukan surat: **tanpa Dear …, tanpa salam penutup**. Laporan punya **judul** dan **judul bagian** (heading: nama pendek di atas setiap bagian), supaya pembaca bisa langsung ke bagian yang ia perlukan:
- **Judul**: *Report on the new English classes for staff*
- **Introduction** (pendahuluan): **tujuan** laporan dalam satu atau dua kalimat: *The aim of this report is to …* / *This report looks at …*
- **Findings** (temuan): fakta dan angka. Kalimat pasif membuatnya objektif: *A survey was conducted …*, *It was found that …*, *Several complaints were received …*. Kata penghubung menunjukkan alurnya: *However, Moreover, As a result,*
- **Recommendations** (rekomendasi): apa yang sebaiknya dilakukan selanjutnya: *The company should …*, *It is recommended that* + subjek + kata kerja (frasa formal yang dihafal saja: *It is recommended that staff use the new app.*)

Beberapa laporan menambahkan **Conclusion** (kesimpulan) sebelum rekomendasi, dan poin-poin (bullet) juga boleh. Tetap **objektif**: fakta dan angka, bukan perasaan (*I think …*, *terrible!!*). Pendapatmu sendiri hanya muncul sebagai rekomendasi.

blocks.text:
**Traps.**
1) Indonesian school and campus reports are long (*BAB I Pendahuluan, Latar Belakang, Rumusan Masalah …*). A short English report goes straight to the point: the Introduction is one or two sentences.
2) Each section has one job: no recommendations in the Findings, no new facts in the Recommendations.
3) Headings are short nouns: *Findings*, not *Here are the things we found*.
4) *The aim of this report is* **to** + verb: *… is to compare two suppliers*, not *is for comparing* ✗.

id.text:
**Jebakan.**
1) Laporan sekolah dan kampus di Indonesia panjang (*BAB I Pendahuluan, Latar Belakang, Rumusan Masalah …*). Laporan singkat bahasa Inggris langsung ke intinya: Introduction cukup satu atau dua kalimat.
2) Setiap bagian punya satu tugas: tidak ada rekomendasi di Findings, tidak ada fakta baru di Recommendations.
3) Judul bagian berupa kata benda pendek: *Findings*, bukan *Here are the things we found*.
4) *The aim of this report is* **to** + kata kerja: *… is to compare two suppliers*, bukan *is for comparing* ✗.

blocks.prompt: This is the whole Findings section of Dimas's report on the office car park: 'I think the car park is a total disaster!!' What is the main problem?
options: It gives a feeling, not facts, and it isn't formal.
It should be under the heading Introduction.
blocks.explain: Findings are **facts and numbers**, written in a calm, objective style: *Only 40% of the spaces are used before 9 a.m. Moreover, several complaints were received about the lights.* *I think*, *a total disaster* and *!!* show a feeling. It isn't an aim either, so it doesn't belong in the Introduction.

id.prompt: Ini seluruh bagian Findings di laporan Dimas tentang tempat parkir kantor: 'I think the car park is a total disaster!!' Apa masalah utamanya?
id.explain: Findings berisi **fakta dan angka**, ditulis dengan gaya tenang dan objektif: *Only 40% of the spaces are used before 9 a.m. Moreover, several complaints were received about the lights.* *I think*, *a total disaster* dan *!!* menunjukkan perasaan. Kalimat itu juga bukan tujuan laporan, jadi tidak cocok di Introduction.

id.intro: Kamu sudah bisa menulis email yang sopan, memilih kata formal dan memakai kalimat pasif. Sekarang kita gabungkan semuanya: email dan surat formal untuk meminta informasi, menyampaikan keluhan dan melamar kerja, dengan pembuka dan penutup yang tepat, plus laporan singkat dengan judul bagian yang jelas.
suggestedQuestions: Kapan aku pakai Yours sincerely dan kapan Yours faithfully?
Apakah salah memakai kalimat aktif di surat formal?
Bagaimana mengatakan 'Dengan hormat' di surat bahasa Inggris?

assessment.fw-1: Tulis ulang kalimat dari pengumuman perusahaan ini dengan register formal: pakai kalimat pasif tanpa pelaku, tense-nya tetap sama, dan tanpa kontraksi. 'We've cancelled the staff conference because of the floods.'
assessment.fw-2: Tulis ulang baris ini untuk email formal kepada klien baru dalam bahasa Inggris: permintaan yang sopan dengan kata-kata lengkap, tanpa singkatan. 'Pls send the docs asap.'
assessment.fw-3: Tulis ulang kalimat pertama email ini untuk sebuah universitas di Australia dengan gaya formal, memakai enquire: 'I want to ask about your scholarships for Indonesian students.'
assessment.fw-4: Kamu menulis surat formal dalam bahasa Inggris British kepada manajer HR sebuah perusahaan di London. Suratnya dimulai dengan 'Dear Ms Carter,'. Salam penutup mana yang dipakai di akhir: Yours sincerely atau Yours faithfully?
assessment.fw-5: Lengkapi kalimat pertama email lamaran kerja ini dengan satu kata (dalam bahasa Inggris): 'I am writing to apply for the position of Sales Executive at PT Maju Jaya, as ___ on JobStreet on 3 June.'
assessment.fw-6: Sebuah laporan singkat tentang bus antar-jemput karyawan punya tiga judul bagian: Introduction, Findings dan Recommendations. Paragraf ini masuk di bawah judul yang mana? Tulis judulnya. 'A second bus should be added at 7 a.m. It is also recommended that drivers check the air conditioning every week.'
assessment.fw-7: Lengkapi kalimat pertama bagian Introduction sebuah laporan dengan satu kata formal (dalam bahasa Inggris): 'The ___ of this report is to compare two cloud storage services and recommend one for the company.'
